summary: Earth Analog Finder is an interactive web app that identifies and classifies different Earth locations on their similarity to the selected Martian or Lunar environments. By comparing geological, climatic, and environmental characteristics, the platform helps the user discover analog terrestrial sites that can support science research, mission planning, education tools and exploration studies.
details:
What does it do?

Earth Analog Finder is an interactive web application that helps discover Earth environments that are similar to the selected locations on Mars and the Moon. The platform analyzes multiple environmental and geological characteristics and ranks terrestrial locations according to their resemblance to extraterrestrial environments.

By adjusting different factors such as temperature, thermal swing, aridity, basalt, iron oxide, roughness, ice, wind & dust, caves/tubes and craters, users can generate customised analog matches and explore how Earth’s extreme environments around the world can be used to study other worlds.

How does it work?

It uses a multi-parameter comparative analysis system that compares Moon and Mars conditions with data from terrestrial analog locations. The user can modify the value assigned to each environmental factor, allowing systems to prioritize specific characteristics depending on the research objective. The algorithm then calculates the similarity scores and produces a ranked list of locations that best match  the selected Martian or Lunar environment.

Interactive visualizations and detailed site information help the users understand why each location is considered an acceptable analog and visualize how different environmental variables influence the match results.

Benefits

  • Makes planetary science data more accessible to students, educators and researchers.
  • Helps identify the suitable locations for mission simulations and technology testing.
  • Encourages the exploration of Earth environments that share characteristics with other planets. 
  • Provides an engaging tool for learning about planetary geology and climate. 

Intended impact

  • The goal of the Earth Analog Finder is to make the relation between planetary exploration and terrestrial research more friendly and accessible. By helping the users understand the similarities between the Earth and extraterrestrial environments, the project impulses the interest in space science, supports educational research and contributes to the identification of analog locations for future research and mission planning.

Technologies Used

  • Python, Html, CSS, and Claude. 
  • At first we tried coding the html file manually, but realized after the second day we weren't going to finish. We asked Claude for help with the formatting of the code, and how we could quickly take out the data from the NASA resources through python.

Creativity

  • Earth Analog Finder combines planetary science and interactive data exploration in a unique way. Instead of presenting predefined information, the platform allows users to customise the variables of comparison criteria and explore Earth locations that are similar to Martian or Lunar environments. Each location is paired by imagery and environmental information, creating a more immersive exploration. This project combines scientific analysis, interactive comparisons and real world photos, making planetary analog research more accessible worldwide. 

Considerations

  • We used Earth, Moon and Mars data ranking various different factors scored from 0-9. We took from NASA POWER climatology the Cold, Thermal swing, Aridity, Wind & Dust for Earth. Whilst Mars and Moon roughness were taken from MGS MOLA and LRO LOLA respectively, and Mars Thermal swing from MGS TES thermal inertia.
  • The rest of the data was estimated rather than taken from a dataset, and based on its environment was given a score from 0-9: Iron oxide, Basalt, Roughness, Ice, Caves/tubes, Craters for Earth, and all remaining factors for the Moon and Mars.
dataRefs: LRO LOLA Gridded Elevation, LDEM_4 (Moon roughness)
MGS TES Thermal Inertia Maps (Mars thermal swing)
